title: Defence Force Retirement Benefits Legislation Amendment (Fair Indexation) Bill 2014
short_title: Defence Force Retirement Benefits Legislation Amendment (Fair Indexation) Bill 2014

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would change how certain military retirement pensions are increased each year for pensioners aged 55 or older.
From 1 July 2014, those pensions would be indexed using the same method as age and service pensions, comparing consumer price index, living cost index and male total average weekly earnings.
The new indexation would apply to DFRB and DFRDB retirement, invalidity and reversionary pensions, but not to child and orphan pensions.
changes: Indexes DFRB and DFRDB pensions for recipients aged 55 or older from 1 July 2014.
Uses the age and service pension indexation method instead of the current CPI-only method.
Applies to retirement, invalidity and reversionary pensions, but excludes child and orphan pensions.
summary.affected: Defence Force Retirement Benefits and Defence Force Retirement and Death Benefits pensioners aged 55 or older, including surviving spouses and associates from family law splits.

speeches.speaker: Christopher Pyne
speeches.brief: Argued Labor's suspension motion was delaying the Defence Force Retirement Benefits Legislation Amendment (Fair Indexation) Bill 2014, which he said would benefit 57,000 veterans who have waited four years for indexation parity with the age pension, as well as the Green Army Programme and unexplained wealth bills.

speeches.speaker: David Feeney
speeches.brief: Argued that the coalition's fair indexation bill is an electoral device given the Howard government refused the same measure for 11 years, quoted a 2007 letter from veterans' advocate John Hevey criticising then minister Bruce Billson, and recalled former finance minister Nick Minchin's public opposition to changing the indexation method.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Nikolic
speeches.brief: Supported the fair indexation bill as a 31-year army veteran, said around 57,000 DFRB and DFRDB superannuants will benefit, and contrasted it with Labor's 2013 election promise, which covered only superannuants aged 65 and over and lacked a wage-based indexation method.

speeches.speaker: Gai Brodtmann
speeches.brief: Supported the fair indexation bill while warning she would oppose it if funded by cuts elsewhere in defence, citing the government's decision to cut a $215 payment to about 1,200 children of veterans and pay cuts of up to $19,000 for ADF personnel serving in Afghanistan and the Middle East.

speeches.speaker: Peter Hendy
speeches.brief: Supported the fair indexation bill, said his electorate of Eden-Monaro has more than 3,500 defence veterans, of whom 813 will directly benefit alongside 132 dependants, and noted a previous coalition attempt to pass similar legislation was defeated by just one vote in the last parliament.

speeches.speaker: Scott Buchholz
speeches.brief: Supported the fair indexation bill, said more than 1,300 people in his electorate of Wright and nearly 19,000 across Queensland will be eligible, and detailed three previous coalition attempts to pass similar legislation blocked by Labor and the Greens in 2011, 2012 and 2013.

speeches.speaker: Karen McNamara
speeches.brief: Supported the fair indexation bill, recounted Central Coast advocate Robert Ihlein's 20-year Army career and campaign for the reform, noted a 2012 pension increase of just $0.81 a fortnight under the old CPI-only method, and said 329 recipients in her electorate of Dobell will benefit.

speeches.speaker: David Coleman
speeches.brief: Supported the fair indexation bill, arguing it reflects the government's priorities after Labor could not fund it despite heavy spending, citing $6½ billion on border protection failures, $100 million from closing live export overnight, and billions wasted on the pink batts program.

speeches.speaker: Craig Kelly
speeches.brief: Supported the fair indexation bill, recalled a memorial service honouring the 287,000 Australians conscripted for national service between 1951 and 1959, and noted the Howard government increased real wages by 21½ per cent during those years, arguing veterans deserve the same recognition in their pensions.

speeches.speaker: Wyatt Roy
speeches.brief: Supported the fair indexation bill, said 1,046 veterans in his electorate of Longman have long campaigned for the reform, and quoted Caboolture-Morayfield and District RSL Sub Branch president Bruce Miller welcoming the government for finally delivering on its election promise.

speeches.speaker: Bob Baldwin
speeches.brief: Supported the fair indexation bill, apologised to veterans for the delay in implementing the reform since the Howard government's Podger review, and questioned why Labor could fund the pink batts and Building the Education Revolution programs but not fair indexation for defence retirees.

speeches.speaker: Ann Sudmalis
speeches.brief: Supported the Defence Force Retirement Benefits fair indexation bill, which will benefit 57,000 military superannuants nationally including almost 1,000 veterans in her electorate of Gilmore, with pensions to be indexed twice yearly in March and September against CPI, living cost and wage benchmarks.

speeches.speaker: Michael McCormack
speeches.brief: Said the fair indexation bill will benefit 57,000 veterans nationally, including 13,699 in New South Wales and 512 in the Riverina, recalling the coalition's commitment dating to 27 June 2010 and Labor and the Greens voting down the same reform in the Senate on 16 June 2011.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Laming
speeches.brief: Read a list into Hansard naming Labor MPs, including Sharon Bird, Anna Burke and Jim Chalmers, who failed to attend the debate on the fair indexation bill, accusing them of abandoning their veteran constituents after only three Labor members showed up to defend the party's record.

speeches.speaker: Dennis Jensen
speeches.brief: Accused Labor of breaking its 2007 promise to release the Podger review and fix military superannuation indexation, said defence spending as a share of GDP fell to levels last seen in 1938 under Labor, and noted the bill will index pensions for 57,000 veterans aged 55 and over from 1 July 2014.

speeches.speaker: Karen Andrews
speeches.brief: Said defence spending fell to just 1.59 per cent of GDP under Labor, the lowest level since 1938, and that the fair indexation bill will benefit 57,000 military superannuants nationally including 483 in her electorate of McPherson, noting her late father was a World War II veteran and advocate for ex-servicemen.

speeches.speaker: Stuart Robert
speeches.brief: Summed up the fair indexation debate, saying the reform benefits 57,000 DFRB and DFRDB members with an immediate impact on 45,000 pensioners aged 55 and over, accused Labor of voting against the measure on three separate occasions, and said Labor's six years in government saw $25 billion cut from the Defence budget.

speeches.speaker: Laurie Ferguson
speeches.brief: Presented a report examining 22 bills and 42 legislative instruments for compatibility with human rights. Raised concerns that national uniform schemes negotiated through COAG can be agreed without formal human rights scrutiny, and sought an update on efforts to address this in drafting protocols for national legislation.

speeches.speaker: Lucy Wicks
speeches.brief: Commended the Minister for Veterans' Affairs for the Defence Force Retirement Benefits Legislation Amendment (Fair Indexation) Bill 2014, which will index DFRB and DFRDB pensions like age and service pensions from 1 July, and cited local veterans among the 56,000 recipients nationally affected by the change.
